stop_condition_text: The anomaly column (certified_disjoint on adjacent pairs) fires at mass in a recorded run — do not 'fix' the dispatch or the census; publish the finding and stop. A disagreement between two landed measurements is the loop's most valuable output.
verdict: STOPPED on stop condition 3. The Phase-1 gate measurement ran on the full corpus (release build) and the anomaly column fired at mass: 4,381 adjacent face pairs were answered exactly `certified_disjoint` by the certified dispatch, concentrated in cylinder~plane (3,600 of 37,361 admitted = 9.6%) and cylinder~cylinder (746 of 5,354 admitted = 13.9%). Adjacent faces share an edge by the census's own enumeration, so an exactly-disjoint certified answer is a representation/admission mismatch: the census's adjacency enumeration and the dispatch's exact admission screens disagree about what a pair IS at corpus scale. Per the packet this disagreement is the loop's most valuable output — the dispatch and the census were deliberately NOT 'fixed'. The certify-rate is 0.5862 (58.6%), far below the 95% floor, and counting the 4,381 disagreements as certified successes flatters the numerator; the Phase-1 exit gate is NOT certified by this run. The doc carries the aggregate verbatim, the per-file table, the per-class breakdown, the anomaly column analysis, the build profile (release), and the reproduction command. Throughput comparison vs the legacy path is DEFERRED TO INTEGRATION per the packet's D-latency fallback: no directly-callable legacy pair-contact entry exists in the test crate.

finding.reading: A cylinder~plane or cylinder~cylinder adjacent pair sharing an edge answered Disjoint thousands of times. The exact screens that produced Disjoint (plane-cylinder: plane parallel to the axis and farther than the radius; cylinder-cylinder: parallel axes farther than r1+r2; sphere-sphere: center distance beyond r1+r2) are reached for pairs the census says touch. This is a landed-measurement disagreement to be investigated at the dispatch/census boundary (compressed-shell edge sharing vs world-space exact screens), not a bug to be papered over.

verification.cargo_fmt_check: clean on the new test file (pre-existing diffs in examples/step_face_timing.rs and tests/geometry_fingerprint.rs are out of scope)

notes: The r1 SPEC_GAP (unreachable pair_dispatch from the look test target) was resolved per the packet's AMENDED r2 section by adding exactly one dev-dependency line to the root Cargo.toml: `truck-certified = { path = "vendor/truck/truck-certified" }`. After that `use truck_certified::pair_dispatch::{dispatch_pair, CertifiedPairParticipant, CertifiedPairResult}` compiles in the look test target, exactly as the amendment predicted. The harness then ran on the corpus. Note the machine's pagefile is small: the release dependency build required -j 2. Latency is per-call wall time of dispatch_pair over the admitted set; a second direct-binary release run produced the same counters with slightly different latency samples (fresh-process variance), and the doc records one canonical release run verbatim.
